The report’s river length and source definition differ in scope from the modeled selection and are not substituted for it.

records.geographic_disambiguation: Lac Duncan and Lac Esprit are supported named components. The neighboring lower Rivière Comb label and a separate Au Castor trip account do not establish one river identity for the selected northern coastal route.
records.completion_scope: All 27 selected parts were considered. The Duncan–Esprit lake passage, downstream joins, lower branching corridor and selected northern coastward branch are supported at ordinary corridor scale. The initial opening and missing westward connector are material geographic gaps; this is not a completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: Named lake components only; no whole-group or northern-terminal river name is adopted.

scope_limits: The selected eastern opening and intermediate headward through-links remain geographically unsupported.

records.region: Kitikmeot, Nunavut, Canada; western Overby Lake map area and the inland approach toward eastern Bathurst Inlet.
records.material_pending_reason: Permitted source cartography has not established the southern opening and its link to the on-sheet feeder, the long westward continuation and northward bend, or the final selected outlet. CHS coastal prose identifies the receiving river and inlet in general but does not connect those descriptions to every selected off-sheet part.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected approach is the narrow southern lake-and-stream feeder west of Overby Lake, joining the westward watercourse printed Hiukitak R. It does not traverse the main basin labeled Overby Lake. Most of the selected western and northern continuation lies outside the inspected sheet, so the coastal description cannot supply the missing through-link.
records.completion_scope: All thirty stored parts of the single selected mainstem fragment were considered. The successfully inspected map establishes the on-sheet southern feeder, its small lake passages, the receiving-river join and the short named westward reach. The chosen opening, off-sheet middle and lower continuation, and actual selected coastal terminal still lack continuous source correspondence. This is one material-pending state, not a completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: The Overby Lake thematic map prints Hiukitak R. on the receiving river at the selected southern feeder's northern join and its short westward continuation. CHS ARC403 independently describes Hiukitak River entering Bathurst Inlet. These observations do not establish a completed identity for the entire selected modeled system.

scope_limits: Hiukitak River is a bounded printed and coastal-prose name observation, not an accepted current official name for the selected whole system.

The selected southern opening, off-sheet middle and lower connections, and actual terminal remain material geographic gaps; they are not requirements for exact bank, vertex or present-flow verification.
The inspected on-sheet feeder includes small unnamed lake passages. No distinct selected lake hydronym or whole-route wetland, glacial, reservoir or managed-water classification is established.
No separate selected tributary fragment exists. Alternative neighboring headwaters and the untraversed Overby Lake are not assigned the candidate river name.
The modeled mainstem length is not represented as an official natural-river length. No verified Korean form, naming date or alias sequence is supplied.

records.region: Northern La Vega tributary approach, lower Camú, lower Yuna and western Bahía de Samaná
records.material_pending_reason: The chosen opening and eastward reach north of La Vega, followed by the southward connector into the Camú corridor, are not continuously identified in the acquired cartography. Municipal prose establishes the Verde–Licey–Camú hierarchy but does not identify the selected opening or its first joins. This is a geographic evidence gap, not a requirement for exact banks or a single name across distinct reaches.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The downstream selection corresponds to the northern, old Yuna outlet toward Sánchez and Bahía de Samaná. It is not assigned to the southern Barracote outlet. Tobey describes the irrigation-cut enlargement that connected Yuna to Barracote in the late 1950s; Herrera-Moreno maps the two outlets separately. The stored sea classification was not treated as independent mouth evidence. The Camú urban course through La Vega does not identify a chosen opening farther north.
records.completion_scope: Bounded research ended with one source-material-pending primary state. Supported downstream Camú/Yuna and the northern Yuna terminal are retained. Completing the finding requires usable independent correspondence for the chosen northern-La Vega opening and southward tributary join, not reopening stopped publications. No source original, derivative image, full coordinate list or acquisition receipt is included in this public-ready finding.
records.supported_name_scope: Yuna is supported for the receiving lower river and northern estuarine outlet near Sánchez. The selection includes a distinct lower Camú approach. The selected opening north of La Vega is not assigned a river name because its correspondence with the Verde–Licey tributary chain is not established.

scope_limits: The entire selected opening and first tributary joins remain unestablished; Verde and Licey cannot be applied merely because that hierarchy is documented in the same district.
Camú and Yuna are distinct named reaches. No scalar name is assigned to all43 parts, even if future opening evidence closes the connected system.

The surviving source dates span1996-map content,2004–2005 project reports,2011 nomination and the2021–2025 municipal plan. They establish ordinary correspondence, not exact present riverbanks, flow shares or operations.
Tobey’s prose includes an early loose association of Rincón with Camú, but its explicit dam section/table identifies Rincón on Jima. The selected route is not asserted to cross that reservoir.
The old Yuna northern mouth is supported by inspected maps and source prose, rather than the selection’s sea flag. Current flow dominance between Yuna and Barracote remains unverified.

publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
